extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive disciplinary standards governing practitioners before the USPTO, including grounds for misconduct (ethical/rules violations), requirements for approving an affidavit of resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, and conditions of exclusion on consent and reinstatement. Targets conduct in preparing/prosecuting patent applications, client communications, fee handling, conflicts, and cooperation with OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a): resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered; not submitted under coercion or duress; respondent is fully aware of implications; respondent is aware that disciplinary proceedings are pending and the nature of the allegations; and the affidavit acknowledges that upon any reinstatement application the Director of Enrollment and Discipline will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of reinstatement, that (a) the facts upon which the complaint is based are true and (b) the respondent could not have successfully defended against the charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director forwards the affidavit to the USPTO Director for review and approval; acceptance results in exclusion on consent. The affidavit must explicitly contain the required acknowledgments to be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion on consent and associated conditions (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an affidavit of resignation is approved, the practitioner may be excluded on consent from practice before the Office; the Director may grant limited recognition (here: 30 days) to wind up client business, and impose conditions such as compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40 (withdrawal/ wind-up procedures), prohibition on accepting new clients, dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates, and requirements for compliance with rules on exclusion and reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order can require specific wind-up steps, publication of the Final Order (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette), notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts, and full compliance with reinstatement procedures (11.60). Respondent must not use USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) – Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, including providing evasive, misleading, or false answers to OED inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples alleged: providing evasive/misleading/false responses to OED about representation and conduct; misrepresenting client communications or firm status. Such conduct supports disciplinary charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) – Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice / neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice; includes neglecting entrusted legal matters and bringing frivolous actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include failing to file non-provisional applications before provisional abandonment, neglecting communications and filings, and bringing frivolous infringement suits or ITC proceedings. Such failures may be deemed prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(2)(ii) – Respondent obligations in inquiries (truthful responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires truthful and non-evasive responses to OED inquiries; prohibits providing evading, misleading, or false answers in the course of disciplinary investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated provision of evasive or misleading answers regarding client representations and applications was specifically alleged across multiple counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) – Demonstrating incompetence
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not demonstrate incompetence in the handling of legal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged incompetence examples include incorrect statements about provisional applications (e.g., asserting a provisional alone provides proof of a prior use date) and failing to understand or explain when priority claims are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b) – Adequate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must handle legal matters with adequate preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged violations include failing to file non-provisionals before provisional abandonment, failing to advise clients about differences between provisional and non-provisional (and design) applications, and generally not preparing adequately for prosecution or litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) – Neglect of entrusted legal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not neglect legal matters entrusted to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include failing to timely return calls, failing to report Notices of Missing Parts to clients, failing to file applications timely before abandonment, and otherwise neglecting client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to advise clients about provisional, non-provisional, and design application differences (as part of competence/communication duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must advise clients that a non-provisional must be filed prior to abandonment of a provisional to claim priority; must explain the difference between provisional and non-provisional (and design vs utility) applications and the impact on patent rights if there is a hiatus between filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to explain these distinctions and risks (e.g., that design applications cannot claim benefit of a provisional) was alleged repeatedly and characterized as incompetence, neglect, and failure of adequate representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) – Accepting compensation from non-client without consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must obtain the client's informed consent after full disclosure before accepting compensation from someone other than the client for services rendered to or for the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged instances include accepting compensation from Aarons & Fleisher or PTI for services to clients without obtaining clients' consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(1) – Revealing confidences or secrets without consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not reveal a confidence or secret of a client without obtaining the client's consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged violations include providing copies of clients' provisional applications to third parties (Aarons & Fleisher, PTI) without client consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.48 – Fee splitting / sharing with non-practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits sharing legal fees with non-practitioners or otherwise engaging in unauthorized fee-splitting arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include sharing portions of client fees with PTI, Aarons & Fleisher, or others who are non-practitioners, and receiving referral/fee payments tied to client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.112(a) and (b) – Maintenance and documentation of client advances in escrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must maintain client funds advanced (e.g., $6,000) in an escrow account separate from the firm's operating account and provide documentation of such maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide documentation that client-advanced funds were maintained in a separate escrow account was alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a) – Declining employment when independent professional judgment likely impaired
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must decline employment when the exercise of independent professional judgment on behalf of a client would likely be affected by representation of another client (i.e., avoid conflicting interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: failing to decline representation where subject matter overlapped with a prior client and potential conflicts existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(b) – Continuing multiple employment without informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must obtain the client's informed consent after full disclosure before continuing multiple employment when independent professional judgment may be adversely affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: continuing to represent clients with overlapping interests without first obtaining consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.47(a) – Aiding unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not aid in the unauthorized practice of law by directing clients to non-lawyer entities to perform legal decision-making or to interpose non-lawyers in legal judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: instructing a client to contact PTI to decide whether to convert a provisional into a non-provisional or to file a non-provisional was characterized as aiding unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(b) – Prohibition on permitting third parties to direct or regulate professional judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to direct or regulate the practitioner's professional judgment in rendering legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: permitting PTI, which referred and paid the practitioner for services, to intercede or direct the client and influence the practitioner's judgment (e.g., payment arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (frivolous litigation) / obligation to avoid frivolous claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not bring frivolous infringement suits or ITC proceedings; such conduct is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: bringing suits and ITC proceedings without sufficient pre-filing investigation or that were frivolous supports discipline under §10.23(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.26(b)(6) – Pre-filing investigation duties in litigation (as cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must perform sufficient pre-filing infringement investigation before filing infringement suits or ITC proceedings; failing to do so may violate professional responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: participating in filing infringement suits and ITC proceedings without sufficient pre-filing investigation and continuing to file additional suits after being put on notice that investigation was insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6) – Habitual and repeated violation of disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in habitual and repeated violations of the disciplinary rules can itself be a ground for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: repeatedly submitting provisional applications that are allowed to abandon and then filing related non-provisional/design applications where priority cannot be claimed was characterized as habitual repeated violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve affidavits of resignation, exclude practitioners, and take disciplinary action is grounded in 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and corresponding 37 C.F.R. provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are taken pursuant to these statutes and implementing regulations and are published in OED's Reading Room and the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and Official Gazette/Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED must publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and may publish a notice in the Official Gazette; notice of public discipline and reasons must be given to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states of admission, courts of admission, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes a Notice of Exclusion on Consent containing summary of charges and the practitioner's exclusion; these notices inform other disciplinary bodies and the public.
